mutations.because: narrowing the dual-key match to the uuid alone (D246, H5) — dropping the slug bind value along with its placeholder — leaves every SLUG-keyed decision/decision_set/report/pool/job row un-deleted — the pinned test plants one row under the campaign's slug key and a separate row under its uuid key for each of the five tables and asserts both counts are zero; under this mutant the slug-keyed report row (and its four siblings) survives, so `expect(count).toBe(0)` fails on that assertion line, not on a thrown error — a clean, non-vacuous witness.
command: deleteCampaignRows frees decision, decision_set, report, pool and job by slug and by the campaigns uuid text

mutations.because: dropping the live-campaign guard in `resolveCampaignForPurge` lets a purge resolve and proceed against a campaign that was never tombstoned — the pinned test plants a campaign with `deleted_at` null and asserts the call rejects; under this mutant it resolves instead, so `rejects.toThrow(/not tombstoned/)` fails on that assertion line, not on a thrown error from elsewhere.

disabling the key-collision refusal lets deleteCampaignRows(A) proceed when A.slug collides with another campaign's id in the same org, so it deletes both A's and B's keyed rows (B.id = A.slug) and A's campaign row instead of refusing — the pinned test asserts a /shares a key/ rejection and that both campaigns' rows survive; under this mutant the rejection never happens and the row-existence assertions fail on an assertion line, not a throw or compile error
command: deleteCampaignRows refuses a campaign whose slug is another campaign's id
